analysis: Examined three changes. (1) WeightHasher.swift: hashSingleFileUncached now calls PageCache.drop(descriptor:) before close (lines 250-253). This is a memory-residency optimization and the digest logic is unchanged. PageCache is not supplied, so its failure behavior is unverified, but it is called in a defer after hashing, so it cannot affect the digest result. (2) Darkbloom.swift lines 171-229: attachWeightHashes gains an optional verifiedWeightHashesFile. The new registrationWeightHash reuses a VerifiedWeightHashStore record only when model.weightsVerifiedByManagedLoad is true and the file identities match. Otherwise it does a full hash and records it for managed-load models. Identities are captured before hashing, matching the fingerprint ordering (lines 188-192), so a file changed mid-hash yields a stale identity and forces a re-hash. The default nil parameter keeps other callers on the full-hash path. (3) StartCommand+Modes.swift line 216-217: runForeground now passes VerifiedWeightHashStore.path() to attachWeightHashes. Security reasoning: the registration weight hash is self-reported by the provider, and a malicious provider can already lie about it (T-012, T-027, and the comment in WeightHasher.snapshotFingerprint). The record store sits on operator-writable disk, so forging it gives an adversarial operator nothing beyond lying directly. For honest providers, the comment says the managed load re-verifies every file's SHA-256 before serving. That is the compensating control that keeps a stale or incorrect reused registration hash from being served. Open items for integration (code not supplied): (a) what VerifiedWeightHashStore.fileIdentities covers (path, size, mtime, inode, or only some of these) and whether it is bound to the full integrity file set from ModelScanner.collectWeightFiles; (b) how the store is validated (file permissions, schema, atomic writes, stale-model handling); (c) that weightsVerifiedByManagedLoad is true only where the load really SHA-256-verifies all files before serving. If any of these is weaker than the comments claim, the hash advertised to the coordinator, and the cache weightHash binding in T-041, could diverge from the bytes actually loaded. No concrete regression is identifiable from the supplied evidence.
